subject: general
question: When was the Pan‑India Fire Safety Week observed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**April 21–25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)** organized the **Pan-India Fire Safety Week** from **April 21 to April 25, 2025**. This initiative was specifically designed to bolster fire prevention mechanisms across all healthcare institutions in the country.
 
• The primary objective of this week was to **sensitize healthcare staff**, including doctors, nurses, and administrative personnel, about the critical nature of fire safety in a clinical environment where patients may be non-ambulatory or vulnerable.
 
• During this period, the **Government of India** directed all **Central Government Hospitals** and **AIIMS** institutions to conduct rigorous **Fire Safety Audits** and **Electrical Load Audits** to prevent short circuits, which are a leading cause of hospital fires.
 
• The observance involved comprehensive **mock drills** conducted in coordination with local **Fire Departments**. These drills simulated emergency evacuation procedures and the effective use of **fire extinguishers** and **hydrant systems**.
 
• Special emphasis was placed on the safety of **Oxygen Plants** and **ICUs (Intensive Care Units)**, ensuring that all life-saving equipment is protected against potential fire hazards through strictly enforced **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is April 21–25.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Fire Service Day:**

 
 
• In **India**, **National Fire Service Day** is observed annually on **April 14**.
 
• It commemorates the brave firemen who lost their lives during the **Victoria Dock explosion** in **Bombay** (now Mumbai) on **April 14, 1944**.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** typically extends this observance into a **Fire Service Week** (usually **April 14–20**), which serves as a precursor to specialized departmental weeks like the one held by the **Health Ministry**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• Fire safety standards in India are governed by the **National Building Code (NBC) 2016**, specifically **Part IV**, which deals with Fire and Life Safety.
 
• Healthcare facilities are classified as **Institutional Buildings** under the code, requiring stringent fire-resistant construction and **Clearance Certificates (NOC)** from the **Fire Service Department**.
 
 
 
• **NDMA Guidelines:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** provides specific guidelines for **Hospital Safety**, emphasizing the need for **disaster management plans** and regular training of "fire marshals" within hospital staff.
 
• These guidelines highlight the importance of **smoke detectors**, **automatic sprinkler systems**, and clearly marked **fire exits** that must remain unobstructed at all times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Causes of Hospital Fires:** Statistics indicate that nearly **75%** of hospital fires in **India** are caused by **electrical short circuits**, often due to overloaded circuits in aging infrastructure or high-power medical machinery.
 
• **Training and Awareness:** The **MoHFW** 2025 initiative mandated that at least **80%** of the on-duty staff at any given time must be trained in basic **firefighting techniques** and **patient evacuation protocols**.
 
• **Reporting Mechanism:** Following the **Fire Safety Week**, all medical superintendents were required to submit a **compliance report** to the **Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS)** confirming the functional status of their fire-fighting equipment.
